title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - CardioLyze
summary: POC scoping call to define success criteria, workload sizing and network setup for a private deployment. Main concerns: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, data residency (EU/US separation), egress restrictions, timeline for a 4-week pilot and benchmarks to validate latency and throughput. Next steps: share private networking checklist, architecture diagram, security pack, and schedule a two-week benchmark run in staging.
next_steps: Jordan to share Redwood private networking checklist + RA profile by 2025-08-14
Priya to propose benchmark matrix and scripts by 2025-08-15
CardioLyze infra to provide VPC CIDR + contact for peering (Miguel) by 2025-08-14
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send private networking checklist, architecture diagram, and SOC2 brief - due 2025-08-14
Priya Nair - Share benchmarking harness (load script + measurement template) - due 2025-08-15
Miguel Torres - Provide VPC CIDR ranges, preferred regions, and whether PrivateLink is required - due 2025-08-14

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-12 15:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Anika Sharma (CTO - CardioLyze), Miguel Torres (Infra), Sonia Patel (Security), Evan Cho (ML eng)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, then deep dive on private networking options and data residency. Define POC success metrics (p95 latency, qps, accuracy baseline), confirm workload size and model choices, and agree timeline for pilot and benchmark run.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time — this is Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:06] Anika Sharma: Hi Jordan, thanks. Doing good. We'll jump in — we mostly want to validate a private setup for inference, data never leaves region, and get some numbers for latency & cost.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Great, that's helpful. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, walk through network options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), sizing (QPS, model, sequence length), then benchmarks and timeline. Sound good?
[00:25] Miguel Torres: Yep. Also we need to know if Redwood needs any outbound egress or if traffic can stay entirely within our VPC.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: Good call. We'll cover egress. Before that — quick qualification: what models are you planning to serve, approximate request size, and expected concurrency?
[00:40] Evan Cho: We're looking at an ensemble: a smaller open model for routing and a 13B-ish model for most responses today; medium term we may test a 70B for higher-quality prompts. Typical sequence length ~512 tokens, average input 80 tokens, output 120 tokens. Peak QPS target for POC: 30-50 QPS, sustained maybe 10-15.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Okay that maps to a medium throughput workload. For 13B models we can hit 30–50 QPS with dedicated instances + batching, latency target?
[01:12] Anika Sharma: We'd like p95 latencies under 300ms if possible for 13B, but we can accept up to 500ms during peaks. Cost target is not strict now but we want to understand unit economics.
[01:22] Priya Nair: That latency goal is tight for 13B with 512 seq depending on batching — we'll lay out the benchmark matrix. For POC we typically do two runs: our micro-bench (single-request latency profile) and a load run to validate p95 under your QPS.
[01:34] Miguel Torres: On networking — our security team strongly prefers no public internet egress for inference traffic. We run in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, and we need EU data to stay in eu-west-1 due to residency rules.
[01:46] Jordan Lee: Understood. We support private deployments in VPC with two options: VPC peering (classic) or AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). Each has tradeoffs.
[01:55] Priya Nair: VPC peering is simple, lower latency inside the same account or between accounts, but transitive routing and cross-region peering adds constraints and you might pay inter-region data transfer. PrivateLink gives you private endpoints and avoids route table complexity but requires ENIs and can be region-scoped; it's also friendlier when customers want to keep tight control over their subnets.
[02:18] Sonia Patel: Important note — we can't allow traffic to egress to a vendor-managed public subnet. If PrivateLink requires a vendor-managed endpoint in our account, that's fine, but we want clear audit logs, mTLS, and keys in our KMS.
[02:33] Priya Nair: We can support customer-managed ENIs and integrate with your KMS. For auditability Redwood sends request-level logs to the private endpoint and you can configure log forwarding to CloudWatch or a SIEM. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[02:47] Jordan Lee: Also note we can run fully private control plane in a Private deployment; in that mode the control plane can be customer-managed and the inference plane stays inside your VPCs. We can sign an addendum for data residency and egress constraints.
[03:02] Anika Sharma: That sounds promising. For region separation — can you guarantee that EU requests are pinned to eu-west-1 nodes?
[03:09] Priya Nair: Yes, routing policies let you pin by region and customer tag. For the POC we'll reserve eu-west-1 capacity so EU traffic never leaves the region.
[03:17] Evan Cho: For benchmarks, can you run our test harness in your dedicated environment, or should we run it from inside our VPC against the PrivateLink endpoint?
[03:25] Priya Nair: We prefer a hybrid: we'll run Redwood's controlled bench from our side to validate baseline, but you'll run your traffic generator inside your VPC so it reflects real network paths. We'll correlate logs.
[03:34] Miguel Torres: On encryption: we need TLS mTLS for all connections and key control via our KMS. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[03:41] Jordan Lee: Yes — customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments. For Hosted we use our key management but can support encryption-at-rest and secure transport; in Private we allow KMS/HSM integration.
[03:52] Priya Nair: Back to success criteria: let's capture concrete metrics for the POC. Proposal from Redwood: 1) p95 latency < 350ms for 13B at 30 QPS with 512 seq (accept up to 500ms as soft fail). 2) Throughput verification: sustained 30 QPS for 30 minutes with error rate < 1%. 3) Quality baseline: no regressions vs your current model (we'll run 200 eval prompts). 4) Security controls: VPC peering or PrivateLink established, KMS integrated, SOC2 report provided.
[04:18] Anika Sharma: That works — I'll add a data residency acceptance: EU traffic must be processed and stored in eu-west-1 only.
[04:25] Sonia Patel: Also need an audit log sample and retention options — 90 days minimum for the POC.
[04:30] Priya Nair: We'll provide sample logs and a retention config. For benchmarks we'll need sample prompts, synthetic load profiles, and your preferred percentiles to measure (p50/p95/p99).
[04:42] Evan Cho: We'll provide a set of 250 prompts and an internal traffic pattern; most requests are short (80 tokens in) but some longer sequences up to 1k tokens.
[04:50] Priya Nair: Good to know about the 1k tail. That will affect memory and KV cache sizing.
[04:55] Jordan Lee: Regarding timeline — proposed: week 0 (this week) finalize network approach and sign a simple NDA/addendum; week 1 (8/19) provisioning and peering/PrivateLink setup; week 2 (8/26) dry-run and small micro-bench; week 3 (9/02) full load bench; week 4 (9/09) results review and decide next steps / scale plan. Does that align?
[05:17] Anika Sharma: Yes, that timeline is acceptable internally. We may need security review which could add a few days but we'll try to be tight.
[05:24] Miguel Torres: A couple of infra clarifications: we'll provide CIDR ranges, and we prefer PrivateLink if it simplifies routing policies and avoids cross-account route table changes. Also ask: does PrivateLink increase latency significantly?
[05:36] Priya Nair: PrivateLink typically adds a few milliseconds of overhead vs peering; in our benchmarks we often see <10ms difference inside the same region. The tradeoff is clearer security boundaries and easier auditing. Inter-region peering will incur inter-region data charges; PrivateLink is region-scoped so for EU you'll still need a separate endpoint in eu-west-1.
[05:57] Sonia Patel: For compliance: we'll need your SOC2 Type II, data processing addendum, SAML/SSO support, RBAC controls, and a description of how you handle logs and redaction if needed.
[06:10] Jordan Lee: We'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report. We also support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. We'll include a short note on how logs can be redacted or forwarded.
[06:20] Anika Sharma: On cost — can you provide a rough expected unit cost for the POC runs? We mainly want to estimate burn.
[06:27] Jordan Lee: We'll create a conservative estimate: for the 13B on Dedicated capacity for a 4-week pilot including reserved nodes for peak we can provide a ballpark in the follow-up email. Priya will also give tips on batching and KV cache to reduce per-token cost.
[06:40] Priya Nair: For the bench matrix I'll propose two model sizes (13B, 70B), different batch sizes, and traffic profiles. We'll capture token cost and latency.
[06:49] Miguel Torres: One more thing — egress billing. We need to verify whether inter-region traffic during your monitoring or control-plane calls will cause egress charges.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: We'll scope that precisely in the checklist. For Private deployments we can keep the control plane also in-region to avoid egress; if you use our hosted control plane there may be some control-plane egress but we can estimate it.
[07:12] Anika Sharma: Cool. Let's capture action items and finalize who does what.
[07:16] Jordan Lee: Action items: Jordan to send network checklist and SOC2, Priya to send bench scripts, Miguel to send CIDRs and preference for PrivateLink, Sonia to confirm data residency specifics, Anika to coordinate security review.
[07:29] Anika Sharma: Sounds good.
[07:31] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the attachments and a calendar invite for the bench kickoff.
[07:36] Miguel Torres: Thanks.

End meeting.
notes: Customer strongly prefers PrivateLink but open to peering if inter-region costs are acceptable
EU data must remain in eu-west-1; customer will provide prompts and internal traffic profile
Bench plan: micro-latency run + load run; Redwood to provide scripts; customer to run generator from their VPC
